region.why: a deployment fact: HCAZERRS ASSIGNs SYSID into the message it writes; the corpus names no region

notes: The example-health-apis visit writer HCAVDB01, LINKed with a COMMAREA: after the length checks it builds a DB2 timestamp from CA-VISIT-DATE and CA-VISIT-TIME and INSERTs a BLOODPRESSURE and a HEARTRATE row. Tables come from the estate's @DB2CRE.jcl (HCZMSA1). Derived from IBM's example-health-apis (github.com/ibm/example-health-apis, Apache-2.0; (C) Copyright IBM Corp. 2011, 2014): LICENSE here is the corpus's own, NOTICE names the source and what was derived.

scenarios.name: add-visit
scenarios.why: EIBCALEN covers the header: one BLOODPRESSURE row and one HEARTRATE row inserted for patient 1, CA-RETURN-CODE '00'

scenarios.name: add-visit-second-time
scenarios.why: a second visit time for the same patient: the key is (patient, timestamp), so both inserts succeed

scenarios.name: no-commarea
scenarios.why: EIBCALEN 0: WRITE-ERROR-MESSAGE (LINK HCAZERRS) then ABEND HCCA

scenarios.name: short-commarea
scenarios.why: one byte under the 18-byte header: '98' to CA-RETURN-CODE, RETURN before any INSERT

scenarios.name: duplicate-bloodpressure
scenarios.why: seed.sql holds a BLOODPRESSURE row for patient 2 at this timestamp: INSERT is -803, '90', the error message is written and the task returns before INSERT HEARTRATE

scenarios.name: duplicate-heartrate
scenarios.why: seed.sql holds only a HEARTRATE row for patient 3 at this timestamp: INSERT BLOODPRESSURE succeeds, INSERT HEARTRATE is -803, '90'
